title: Rayong With Kids: 3-Day Family Plan (Aquarium, Beaches, Koh Samet) | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 3-day, 2-night Rayong family itinerary for travelers with young kids — the aquarium, calm shallow beaches, and a day on Koh Samet, with real opening hours, entry fees, and ferry prices.
keywords: Rayong with kids, Rayong family itinerary, Rayong aquarium, Koh Samet with kids, shallow beaches Rayong Thailand
h1:
Rayong With Kids: 3 Days, 2 Nights
Aquarium, Shallow Beaches, Koh Samet
intro: Rayong is one of the easiest stretches of coast near Bangkok to bring small kids to — just a few hours' drive and you're there. You get an air-conditioned aquarium where kids can watch fish out of the sun, gently sloping shallow beaches where the water's calm enough to relax, and Koh Samet just a 30-minute boat ride away. We've built a 3-day, 2-night plan that keeps the driving short, leaves room for naps, and times each activity around when places actually open.

blocks.html: When you take little kids to the beach, the two things you worry about most are strong waves and harsh midday sun. Rayong handles both well: several mainland beaches slope gently with calm water, and there are indoor options like the aquarium to duck out of the heat at noon. This plan keeps day one light so everyone can settle in, sends you out to Koh Samet on day two, then leaves the last day for souvenirs before you head home.

items: Best season — Nov–Apr brings clear water and small waves, the best time to let kids swim. During the rainy season the surf picks up, so always check the beach warning flags.
Getting around — A private car is by far the easiest for families with a car seat and a lot of kids' gear. From Bangkok it's about a 3-hour drive via the motorway to Rayong town.
Where to stay — Base yourself around Mae Ramphueng Beach or Ban Phe to be close to both the aquarium and the pier for Koh Samet, which cuts down the kids' time in the car.
What to pack — Kids' sunscreen, hats, swim rings, non-slip water shoes, and a spare set of clothes in case they get soaked.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Arrive in Rayong · aquarium · easy evening on the beach

items.activity: Arrive in the Ban Phe area, check in or drop your bags first
items.note: Leaving Bangkok in the morning gets you here mid-morning, before the kids get cranky

items.activity: Lunch at a seafood spot around Ban Phe
items.note: Order something mild for the kids, like steamed sea bass with soy sauce or a crab omelette

items.activity: Visit the Rayong Aquarium and watch the sea fish in the air-conditioning
items.note: Open Wed–Fri 10:00–16:00 · Sat–Sun/holidays 10:00–17:00 · closed Mon–Tue · adults 30 THB, kids under 15 are 10 THB, kids under 120 cm tall are free

items.activity: Head back so the kids can nap, then hit Mae Ramphueng Beach in the softer afternoon light
items.note: Play in the sand in the evening when the sun isn't strong; there are restrooms and showers along the beach

items.activity: Catch the sunset by the shore and have dinner at a beachfront restaurant
items.note: Plenty of places have tables right on the sand, so the kids can run around while the food comes

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Koh Samet · shallow water at Sai Kaew Beach

items.activity: Go to Ban Phe pier, park the car, and take the boat to Koh Samet
items.note: Parking is around 50 THB/day · the regular ferry is 70 THB each way, about 30 min · a speedboat is 200 THB each way, about 10 min · kids aged 0–5 ride free

items.activity: Arrive on the island, pay the park entry, and head straight to Sai Kaew Beach
items.note: Island entry is 40 THB for Thai nationals, free for kids and seniors 60 and over · Sai Kaew has fine white sand, clear water, and few rocks, which makes it great for kids to wade into

items.activity: Swim and play in the sand at Sai Kaew Beach
items.note: Pick a spot where the water is shallow and the waves are gentle, put sunscreen on the kids before they go in, and have them drink water often to beat the heat

items.activity: Break for lunch at a beachfront restaurant and get out of the worst of the midday sun
items.note: Avoid swimming from 12:00–15:00 when the sun is strongest, and let the kids rest in the shade

items.activity: Get back in the water in the late afternoon, or stroll over to the next bay
items.note: Ao Phai just next door is also clear and swimmable, and quieter than Sai Kaew

items.activity: Take the boat back to Ban Phe pier before evening
items.note: Heading back before dark makes it easier to carry the kids on and off the boat, and leaves time in case there's a line for the ferry

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Tung Prong Thong · souvenirs at Ban Phe Market

items.activity: Go to Tung Prong Thong at Pak Nam Prasae and walk the boardwalk through the mangroves
items.note: Open daily 06:00–18:00, free entry · parking 20 THB · the boardwalk is an easy walk, a stroller can manage some stretches, and the wetland looks best from 11:00–15:00

items.activity: Grab lunch in the Pak Nam Prasae community or head back to Ban Phe
items.note: Fresh seafood at friendly prices; kids can have fish rice porridge or steamed egg

items.activity: Wander Ban Phe Market and pick up dried seafood souvenirs
items.note: The market is open roughly 09:00–16:00, with dried shrimp, dried squid, fish sauce, and snacks to take home before you leave
Leaving in the early afternoon gets you back to Bangkok before evening and ahead of the rush-hour traffic

blocks.title: Tips for bringing kids to Rayong
blocks.html: The aquarium is closed Monday–Tuesday, so if your trip lands on the start of the week, swap in the indoor activity on a day it's open — or do Ban Phe Market instead and save the aquarium for a day it's actually running.

blocks.text: Why Rayong works for little kids

items.name: Close, short drive
items.blurb: About 3 hours from Bangkok, so the kids aren't stuck in the car long enough to melt down, with easy gas-station bathroom stops along the way

items.name: Gentle, shallow beaches
items.blurb: Mae Ramphueng and Sai Kaew are easy to wade into with few rocks, though you should still watch the warning flags when the surf is up

items.name: Indoor options too
items.blurb: The air-conditioned aquarium is there to escape the midday sun, so you can alternate with outdoor time instead of baking all day

blocks.html: One thing worth saying plainly: weekends and long holidays get very crowded, both the boats to Koh Samet and Sai Kaew Beach itself. If you can go on a weekday, it's a lot more relaxed — shorter ferry lines and less packed sand, which is much easier when you're watching small kids.

faq.q: How many days is right for visiting Rayong with young kids?
faq.a: Three days and two nights is just about perfect — you get the aquarium, the mainland beaches, and a day over on Koh Samet without cramming so much in that the kids wear out. If you only have 2 days, drop the Koh Samet day and stick to the mainland.

faq.q: What days is the Rayong Aquarium open, and how much is entry?
faq.a: It's open Wed–Fri 10:00–16:00 and Sat–Sun/public holidays 10:00–17:00, closed Mon–Tue. Entry is 30 THB for adults and 10 THB for kids under 15; kids under 120 cm tall and seniors 60 and over get in free.

faq.q: Can you take small kids to Koh Samet, and is the boat ride long?
faq.a: Yes. The regular ferry from Ban Phe pier takes about 30 minutes and a speedboat about 10. Kids aged 0–5 ride free, and island entry is 40 THB for Thai nationals (free for kids and seniors 60 and over). We'd point you to Sai Kaew Beach for its shallow water and gentle waves, which suit kids well.

faq.q: Which Rayong beach is best for kids to swim at?
faq.a: Sai Kaew Beach on Koh Samet has clear water, fine sand, and few rocks. On the mainland, Mae Ramphueng is also swimmable and has restrooms and showers ready to go. But at every beach, watch the warning flags and stay out when the surf is strong.

faq.q: Is Tung Prong Thong manageable on foot with kids?
faq.a: Yes — there's a flat nature boardwalk that's an easy walk, and a stroller can manage some of it. It's open daily 06:00–18:00 with free entry; you only pay 20 THB for parking. The wetland is greenest and best from 11:00–15:00.
